episode_title: 25 Years of Coaching Lawyers: What Drives Profit, Focus, and Growth with Glenn Finch | Ep 204

real_qa.q: What are the three main strategies to improve net income profitability in a law practice according to Glenn Finch at Atticus?
real_qa.r: Glenn recommends: first, value yourself and what you do so you charge appropriately and attorneys believe their services matter; second, hire high-performing people because employee quality directly drives profitability and you must be ready to continuously upgrade your team; third, learn to say no to clients you settled for and work only with your best clients to avoid clogging capacity with time wasters and raising your average value profile.
real_qa.requete: law firm profitability strategies Glenn Finch Atticus

real_qa.q: How did Glenn Finch balance 28 years of Florida National Guard service while working 25 years at Atticus as a practice advisor?
real_qa.r: Glenn joked he was like Halley's Comet at Atticus, disappearing for a year on deployments and returning to rebuild the coaching practice several times. Despite this challenge, he became one of Atticus's top-producing advisors and leads both the Trial Lawyers Group and Practice Growth Program Group. He extended his military service by two years at the Adjutant General's request before asking to finish six months earlier, balancing both careers by applying military education principles to his coaching work.
real_qa.requete: Glenn Finch 28 years military National Guard Atticus dual career

real_qa.q: What is Glenn Finch's approach to helping lawyers get unstuck when they feel stuck in their practice or life?
real_qa.r: Glenn focuses on identifying limiting beliefs as the root cause of being stuck. He discovered about 15 years ago that when lawyers get stuck, it is usually somewhere in their beliefs—such as believing poor hires are all that exists, or that past failures mean things cannot work. He recommends flipping the script by helping clients believe that good people are out there, time blocking works, and cultivating gratitude for what they have, which frees them to make progress.
real_qa.requete: getting unstuck beliefs Glenn Finch coaching lawyers

real_qa.q: Why is learning to say no to clients a critical profitability strategy according to Atticus coaching?
real_qa.r: Working less with clients you settled for and only working with better clients you can find increases profitability because settling clogs up your capacity with time wasters and lowers your average value profile. By overcoming the fear of losing the next dollar and staying completely focused on your dream A-client, attorneys who are serious about targeting the right clients watch their average value climb steadily—one of the best KPIs that you can affect immediately.
real_qa.requete: saying no to clients profitability law practice

real_qa.q: What is the Florida National Guard and how does it differ from active duty military service?
real_qa.r: The Florida National Guard is Component 2 of three Army components, with active duty as Component 1 and Army Reserve as Component 3. The National Guard has the same training, requirements, and promotional requirements as active duty, but serves both the U.S. federal government when called and the state governor on state active duty for emergencies like riots, fires, hurricanes, and immigration efforts, making it a unique dual-service role.
real_qa.requete: Florida National Guard component active duty difference

real_qa.q: What does Sean Achor's book The Power of Beliefs say about the seven core beliefs needed for success and getting unstuck?
real_qa.r: Sean Achor's book, published this year, identifies seven core beliefs that if reignited would unlock success, innovation, and accomplishment. Glenn references that one core belief is that no matter what the day holds or how bad it has been, there is always something to be grateful for, and that people must believe their behavior and choices matter day to day in order to stop accepting being stuck as the norm.
real_qa.requete: Sean Achor Power of Beliefs seven core beliefs success

guest.bio_context: Glenn Finch spent 28 years in distinguished service with the Florida National Guard, retiring on October 31st, while simultaneously serving 25 years as a practice advisor at Atticus coaching high-performing attorneys. He was promoted to colonel in 2018 and served as a Special Staff Officer of the Adjutant General of Florida at Joint Force Headquarters, managing both air and army operations. His dual careers in military leadership and law firm coaching uniquely positioned him to advise on team building, profitability, and high-performance management across two demanding fields.
